newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Pen says Chirac should resign if fails in vote.
newsitem.headline: Le Pen says Chirac should resign if fails in vote.

text.p: French extreme-rightist leader Jean-Marie Le Pen said on Wednesday that President Jacques Chirac should follow an example set by Charles de Gaulle and resign if his backers do badly in next month's parliamentary elections.
Although he was not legally bound to do so, president De Gaulle resigned in April 1969 when a majority voted in a referendum against his proposal for regional reform.

"Chirac is also presenting this election like a plebiscite. What one will have to look at on the evening of the first round is the amount of votes which go to the his backers," said Le Pen, head of the National Front.

"If they get not even half, perhaps not even a third of all votes cast, then I think he should draw the consequences of his failure like de Gaulle did and he should go," Le Pen said in an interview with LCI television.
Even if parties of the ruling centre-right coalition lose the election to the left-wing opposition, Chirac would not be obliged to resign. His term runs to 2002.
Opinion polls indicate that Chirac's backers will get about 45 percent of the votes in the May 25 first round but win in the June 1 run-off.
Le Pen said his own National Front party will field 570 candidates but would not say if he would be a candidate himself.
Analysts say Le Pen will probably not run for fear of being beaten while several of his would-be successors in the FN might be elected.
Le Pen wants to expel several million foreigners from France and he said both left and right mainstream parties had agreed to keep immigration out of the campaign.
